A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSW-SL research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original gradient-flow, image color-transfer, and generative-model experiments, including numerical results and generated images.

after.justification: Original experiments are retained, with additional high-dimensional gradient-flow, STL-10 GAN, and diffusion-model results in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The tree-system and Radon-transform construction is retained, but v2 adds a diffusion-training adaptation using TSW-SL inside the augmented generalized mini-batch energy objective (Appendix E.4). MaxTSW-SL pseudocode also changes: v2 Algorithm 3 updates the root direction and normalizes directions after updates, unlike v1 Algorithm 4.

E1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian target distributions in 10, 50, 75, 100, 150, and 200 dimensions, plus STL-10 image generation at 96×96 resolution. Swiss Roll, 25 Gaussians, CIFAR-10, CelebA, and color transfer remain covered; CIFAR-10 GAN results move to Appendix E.3.

E2.justification: v2 adds Orthogonal-SW to the STL-10 comparison and DDGAN and SW-DD to the diffusion comparison. Conversely, eight color-transfer comparators from v1 Figure 5 disappear, including GQSW, RGQSW, and RRGQSW. The original gradient-flow comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Color transfer changes from a reported 1000 iterations and step size 1 to 2000 iterations, with step size 16 for the proposed methods and 1 for baselines. New protocols include 1800-epoch diffusion training with 10000 total projection directions and high-dimensional flows using learning rates 0.05 for TSW-SL versus 0.005 for baselines. These descriptions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a dedicated STL-10 comparison of three, four, and five lines per tree at approximately 50 total directions, extending the three/five-line configurations already examined in v1. Appendix E.4 also adds an analysis of diffusion FID trajectories over training epochs.

E5.justification: Both versions report gradient-flow averages over ten runs and GAN scores over three runs with ± values. v2 extends these existing reporting practices without adding seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a stated increase in repeated runs. Diffusion results provide point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial high-dimensional, STL-10, ablation, and diffusion results. Its Table 4 reports FID values of 3.64, 2.90, and 2.83 for DDGAN, SW-DD, and TSW-SL-DD. Original Table 1 and CIFAR-10/CelebA GAN scores are retained. Additional color-transfer results disappear with v1 Figure 5, including RGQSW and RRGQSW scores of W2=0.01.

T1.justification: v2 specializes the TSW-SL and MaxTSW-SL definitions and metric proofs from general p≥1 to p=1, removing the Sobolev-transport discussion. It also explicitly adds nonnegativity to the splitting-simplex definition. The underlying tree construction, metrizability, and Radon-injectivity arguments are largely retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain tree systems, an injective Radon-transform variant, and an efficiently computable distance generalizing SW. However, v2's headline contributions omit v1's explicit claim of resolving existing TSW's bounded-support limitation and no longer list MaxTSW-SL as a headline contribution, although the variant remains in the paper.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new high-dimensional results as evidence of topology preservation and diffusion FID as evidence of better divergence measurement (Sections 6.1 and E.4). It also explicitly qualifies its ambitions: comparisons primarily target original SW, and outperforming newer SW variants is not expected.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands dataset-generation instructions, sample counts, learning rates, color preprocessing, and architecture details. v2 also documents root placement near the data mean and diffusion computation on two A100 GPUs taking 81.5 hours per run. Conversely, the three direct adapted-code repository links supplied in v1 are removed.

R1.justification: The introduction reframes positioning around replacing SW integration domains, adding discussion of geometric and subspace approaches such as Bonet et al. (2023) and Paty and Cuturi (2019). This replaces much of v1's critique of support-dependent TSW sampling. Diffusion and energy-distance literature is added, while Sobolev-transport and UniFrac references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the methodological and experimental narrative are rewritten. v2 adds a notation glossary, reorganizes Section 6, moves color transfer and CIFAR-10 GAN results to the appendix, reverses the order of the Max-variant and proof appendices, and places references before the supplement. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout and adds a Radon/splitting illustration, dataset scatterplots, a diffusion learning curve, and new comparison tables. The original GAN table is divided across main text and appendix. v1 Figure 4 becomes v2 Figure 6, while the larger v1 Figure 5 montage is removed; the original tree illustrations and generated samples remain.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition, corrected MaxTSW-SL pseudocode, expanded implementation details, and new experiments benefit v2. However, it removes color-transfer evidence where RGQSW and RRGQSW achieved W2=0.01 versus TSW-SL's 24.8. It also retains the identical color-transfer figure despite changing reported iterations from 1000 to 2000 and the proposed method's step size from 1 to 16. The gains coexist with lost comparative evidence and unresolved protocol consistency, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
